learning_outcomes.text: Obtain a general overview of the fundamental concepts of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer.
Acquire the ability to apply the acquired knowledge to solve practical questions and engineering-related problems.
Comprehensively analyze the results for appropriate decision-making.

syllabus_topics: Applications with combined conduction, convection, and radiation
Variation of energy stored by an open system
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Nozzles
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Diffusers
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Venturi meters
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Pipes
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Pumps
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Compressors
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Turbines
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Boilers
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Heat exchangers
Applications of the First Law in open systems: Solar collectors
Previous concepts: heat source, heat engine, and heat pump
Application to heat engines, heat pumps, and refrigeration machines
Mathematical formulation of the Second Law for reversible processes
Calculation of entropy variations in reversible processes
Relationship between heat and work involved in a process by reversible and irreversible means
Mathematical formulation of the Second Law for irreversible processes
Exergy of a closed system in the presence of a single heat source
Exergy of an open system in steady state
The Carnot cycle as a comparative cycle in heat engines
Efficiencies of other gas turbine cycles
Comparison of Diesel cycle with Otto cycle

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical/practical final exam and/or cumulative/eliminatory partial exams
Performance in practical activities (classroom, laboratory, computer lab, field, visits, etc.)
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary call consists of a theoretical/practical exam (80%), practical activities (8%), problem-solving (8%), and attendance (4%). A minimum score of 4.5/10 in the exam component is mandatory for other activities to be counted, and students must achieve a minimum of 3.5/10 in each part of the split exam if the partial is eliminated. In the extraordinary call, only an exam accounts for 80%, while practical activity and problem-solving grades are saved for one academic year. Students choosing global evaluation will have an 80% exam and a 20% practical computer test. If the final grade is above 4 but the established criteria are not met, the final grade in the record will be 4.
